events.title: Democratisation: closed autocracy to electoral autocracy
events.detail: Derived from a change in the Regimes of the World classification, which is itself built from V-Dem expert ratings. It marks the year a country crossed a threshold, not a specific law or decision.
events.source: derived: Regimes of the World / V-Dem
events.contested: Threshold classifications move in a single step, so the date reflects when a gradual change crossed a line rather than when it began. Read the continuous V-Dem indices alongside this to see the underlying trend.

events.title: Democratic opening: electoral democracy index rose 0.25 over 5 years
events.detail: From 0.46 in 1918 to 0.72 in 1923. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.

events.title: Thatcher government takes office
events.detail: The incoming government shifted to monetary targeting, raised VAT while cutting income tax rates, removed exchange controls in October 1979, and began privatising state-owned industries from 1981.
events.contested: Inflation fell and productivity growth improved in some sectors; unemployment rose above three million and regional and income inequality widened sharply. How much of the manufacturing decline was policy and how much was the North Sea oil-driven exchange rate is a long-running argument.
events.refs: ["HM Treasury, Medium Term Financial Strategy (1980)", "Crafts, 'Forging Ahead, Falling Behind and Fighting Back' (2018)"]

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 10%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 47,867 to 42,985 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.
